{{no footnotes|date=May 2016}}
In [[mathematics]], an '''Igusa group''' or '''Igusa subgroup''' is a [[subgroup]] of the [[Siegel modular group]] defined by some congruence conditions. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Igusa|authorlink=Jun-Ichi Igusa|year=1964}}.

==Definition==

The [[symplectic group]] Sp<sub>2''g''</sub>('''Z''') consists of the [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]]
:<math>\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D \end{pmatrix}</math>
such that ''AB<sup>t</sup>'' and ''CD<sup>t</sup>'' are [[symmetric matrix|symmetric]], and ''AD<sup>t</sup>'' − ''CB<sup>t</sup>'' = ''I'' (the [[identity matrix]]). 

The Igusa group Γ<sub>g</sub>(''n'',2''n'') = Γ<sub>''n'',2''n''</sub> consists of the matrices 
:<math>\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D \end{pmatrix}</math>
in Sp<sub>2''g''</sub>('''Z''') such that ''B'' and ''C'' are congruent to 0 mod ''n'', ''A'' and ''D'' are congruent to the identity matrix ''I'' mod ''n'', and the diagonals of ''AB<sup>t</sup>'' and ''CD<sup>t</sup>'' are congruent to 0 mod 2''n''.
We have Γ<sub>g</sub>(2''n'') ⊆ Γ<sub>g</sub>(''n'',2''n'') ⊆ Γ<sub>g</sub>(''n'') where Γ<sub>g</sub>(''n'') is the subgroup of matrices congruent to the identity modulo ''n''.
